#Emily's question (2)
Are lower-paying jobs more vulnerable to AI disruption, or does AI disproportionately threaten high-wage cognitive roles?

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)

df <- read_csv("ai-career-threat-index.csv")

df_clean <- df %>%
  mutate(
    mid_salary = (salary_low_usd + salary_high_usd) / 2,
    income_tier = case_when(
      mid_salary < 60000 ~ "Low Income (<$60k)",
      mid_salary >= 60000 & mid_salary < 120000 ~ "Middle Income ($60k-$120k)",
      mid_salary >= 120000 ~ "High Income (>$120k)"
    ),
    income_tier = factor(income_tier, levels = c("Low Income (<$60k)", "Middle Income ($60k-$120k)", "High Income (>$120k)")),
    risk_level = factor(risk_level, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"))
  )
jobs_to_label <- df_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(score)) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  bind_rows(
    df_clean %>% arrange(desc(mid_salary)) %>% slice(1:3)
  ) %>%
  distinct(title, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Visual 1
# Calculate the correlation and format it as text
cor_val <- cor(df_clean$mid_salary, df_clean$score, use = "complete.obs")
cor_label <- paste0("Pearson R = ", round(cor_val, 2))

scatter_plot_nice <- ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = mid_salary, y = score)) +
  # Add points
  geom_point(aes(color = risk_level, size = tasks_at_risk_count), alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # Add linear regression line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "navy", fill = "coral", linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Add labels for outliers
  geom_text_repel(
    data = jobs_to_label,
    aes(label = title),
    size = 3.5,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    force = 2,
    segment.color = "salmon",
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  
  # ADD CORRELATION MANUALLY HERE (Replaces stat_cor)
  annotate("text", x = 160000, y = 95, label = cor_label, size = 5, fontface = "bold", color = "navy") +
  
  # Formatting
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "pink", "Moderate" = "darkgreen", "High" = "khaki", "Very High" = "orchid")) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 6), guide = "none") + 
  
  labs(
    title = "The Wage-Wipeout Curve: AI Threat vs. Salary",
    subtitle = "Overall, higher-paying jobs face less AI threat, but specific high-wage cognitive roles are heavily exposed.",
    x = "Salary Midpoint (USD)",
    y = "AI Threat Score (0-100)",
    color = "AI Risk Level",
    caption = "Data Source: AI Career Threat Index. Note: Point size indicates tasks at risk."
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "salmon", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(scatter_plot_nice)

# Visual 2
distribution_plot_nice <- ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = income_tier, y = score, fill = income_tier)) +
  
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, trim = FALSE, color = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA, color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5, color = "navy") +
  
  # Add a red diamond for the mean score
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 4, color = "salmon", fill = "salmon") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Low Income (<$60k)" = "pink", 
                               "Middle Income ($60k-$120k)" = "pink", 
                               "High Income (>$120k)" = "pink")) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of AI Threat Scores by Income Tier",
    subtitle = "Lower-income roles face a significantly higher median and mean AI threat (Red Diamond = Mean).",
    x = "Income Tier",
    y = "AI Threat Score (0-100)",
    fill = "Income Tier",
    caption = "Note: Each dot represents a specific job title."
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "navy", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    legend.position = "none", 
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )
print(distribution_plot_nice)



ggsave("Person2_Scatter_Plot.png", plot = scatter_plot_nice, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)

ggsave("Person2_Boxplot.png", plot = distribution_plot_nice, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

#Reuel's question (4)
When combining sector, compensation, and job classification together, what key interaction drives AI risk—and how do those insights tie our report together?
```{r}
ai_df<- read_csv("ai-career-threat-index.csv")
soc_df <- read_csv("soc-crosswalk.csv")

head(ai_df)
names(ai_df) #main id = soc_code (15-1232)
barplot(colSums(is.na(ai_df)),
        las = 2) # the NA values are for the quarterly information 


head(soc_df)
names(soc_df) #main id = soc_code (11-1011)
barplot(colSums(is.na(soc_df)),
        las = 2)

#check to see if the join will work before i adjust the values in the df
PK_code <- intersect(ai_df$soc_code,soc_df$soc_code)

length(PK_code) #248
length(setdiff(ai_df$soc_code,soc_df$soc_code))
nrow(ai_df) #300

nrow(soc_df) #867
length(unique(soc_df$soc_code)) #867

#?left_join()
threat_df <- left_join(ai_df,
                       soc_df, 
                       by = "soc_code")
names(threat_df)

 rename(threat_df$score.x,threat_df$score.y)

#merge score & risk level
threat_df <- threat_df %>% 
  rename(score = score.x,
         risk_level= risk_level.x) %>%
  select(-score.y,-risk_level.y)
#?case_when
threat_df <- threat_df %>%
  mutate(
    mid_salary = (salary_low_usd + salary_high_usd) / 2,
    risk_level = factor(risk_level, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High")),
    income_tier = case_when(
      mid_salary < 60000 ~ "Low Income (<$60k)",
      mid_salary >= 60000 & mid_salary < 120000 ~ "Middle Income ($60k-$120k)",
      mid_salary >= 120000 ~ "High Income (>$120k)"
    ),
    income_tier = factor(income_tier, levels = c("Low Income (<$60k)", "Middle Income ($60k-$120k)", "High Income (>$120k)")),
    tier = factor(tier, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Tier 1", "Tier 2"))
  )

table(threat_df$income_tier)
table(threat_df$category)
table(threat_df$tier)
head(threat_df)

#models
heatmap_df <- threat_df %>%
  group_by(category,income_tier) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(heatmap_df)

heatmap_plot <- ggplot(heatmap_df, aes(x = income_tier, y = reorder(category, mean_score), fill = mean_score)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(mean_score, 1), " (n=", n, ")")), size = 3.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Low Income\n(<$60k)", "Middle Income\n($60k-$120k)", "High Income\n(>$120k)")) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2b8cbe", mid = "#fee08b", high = "#d73027", midpoint = 50) +
  labs(title = "AI Threat Score by Sector & Income Tier", x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Avg Score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(heatmap_plot)

#linear regression

model_base <- lm(score ~ mid_salary, data = threat_df)
summary(model_base)

model_trio <- lm(score ~ mid_salary + category + tier, data = threat_df)
summary(model_trio)

#Does the effect of Salary depend on Sector & Tier?
model_int <- lm(score ~ mid_salary * category + tier, data = threat_df)
summary(model_int)

anova(model_base,model_trio,model_int)

interaction_plot <- ggplot(threat_df, aes(x = mid_salary / 1000, y = score, color = tier)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.65, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ category, ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "How Salary & Job Tier Interact to Drive AI Threat Across Sectors",
    subtitle = "Regression slopes differ sharply by industry (ANOVA Interaction p = 4.86e-06)",
    x = "Midpoint Annual Salary ($ Thousands)",
    y = "AI Threat Score (0–100)",
    color = "SOC Tier"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

print(interaction_plot)
```
